item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports combining item semantics with behavioral embeddings, but the retrieved papers do not establish an exact lightweight, jointly trained-from-scratch BERT4Rec recipe. [DenseRec (2025)](https://earl-workshop.github.io/pdf/recsys2025-workshops_paper_167.pdf) investigates dense content embeddings for sequential Transformers, largely motivated by pretrained representations. [Q-BERT4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02474) combines semantic feature injection, quantization and masked sequence learning; its multimodal, multistage design exceeds this task’s available inputs. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) learns textual item representations through masked representation prediction and two-stage training, offering related motivation rather than a directly matching implementation.\n\nA task-compatible hypothesis inferred from these approaches: tokenize public titles/descriptions; learn random word embeddings, masked mean pooling and a small projection jointly with BERT4Rec; fuse that representation with each item’s ID embedding inside one network. Shared words could connect related items despite sparse co-occurrence, though gains remain unverified. Crucially, replace both ID and text features at every masked target with the reserved mask representation; exposing target text would leak identity. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s Cloze objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), append a mask for inference, and read its final nonpadding position. This yields one jointly trained predictor per category without pretrained weights or separate semantic scoring models."}
